Content: Ming has a unique monarchy form with fixed empire rank and fixed dynasty called the Celestial Empire, reflecting the Chinese belief that a well-governed empire was evidence of divine sanction and blessing, whereas a poorly governed or tyrannical one was evidence that the Emperor could be deposed. 
With Mandate of Heaven, the Celestial Empire represents Ming being the Emperor of China in 1444, a fact that alters gameplay far beyond what is described here, and it may lose or regain this government form like other eligible nations.

Actually I have enough info. Let me synthesize this into a clear answer.

Key points:
1. **Requirements** (potential condition in the game file):
   - **With Mandate of Heaven DLC**: You must be the **Emperor of China** (`is_emperor_of_china = yes`)
   - **Without Mandate of Heaven DLC**: You must either already have the reform OR be in the **Chinese culture group** (`east_asian`) with at least **50 cities**
   - In both cases, the global flag marking that the empire has been dismantled must not be active

For effects, this reform grants monthly prestige, reduces influence across all three estates, boosts governing capacity substantially, locks the government type in place, grants a special casus belli to unify China, blocks the ability to force tributaries, and unlocks factions tied to temples.

With the Mandate of Heaven DLC, it also enables Eunuchs and Bureaucrats factions, fixes the government at rank 3, assigns 90% of territory to estates, and swaps in the Meritocracy mechanic while clearing the standard faction list — and Tier 1 gets permanently locked once chosen, blocking normal conversion away from it. There's also an older legacy version predating the DLC that instead offers prestige alongside increased embracement cost and a smaller governing capacity boost.

The full version outright requires holding the Emperor of China title from MoH, granting far more governing capacity and cutting influence across all three estates, whereas the legacy variant is a weaker fallback that can't even be picked in the nation designer. I'm also puzzling over the `allow_force_tributary = no` flag, since it seems to conflict with what I'd expect from China's historical tribute system, so I want to cross-check that against the wiki's description of the "Too powerful" trade company penalty.

Here's a full breakdown of the **Celestial Empire** government reform, sourced from «Celestial Empire» (game_file, v1.37.3) and «Emperor of China» / «Ming» (wiki).

---

## Requirements (Who Can Take It)

The reform is gated by a **potential condition** that varies by DLC:

| Condition | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **With Mandate of Heaven DLC** | You must currently be the **Emperor of China** (i.e., hold the Mandate of Heaven) |
| **Without Mandate of Heaven DLC** | You must either already have the reform, *or* be of the **East Asian culture group** with at least **50 cities** |
| **Universal blocker** | The global flag `empire_of_china_dismantled` must NOT be active (if the EoC title has been permanently abolished in the world, this reform becomes unavailable to everyone) |

Additionally, for the **Nation Designer**, you need:
- **Chinese culture group** (`east_asian`) + **Chinese tech group**
- Capital located in the **North China**, **Xinan**, or **South China** region (costs +1000% in the designer)

---

## What It Does

### Modifiers
- **+0.5** Monthly Prestige
- **+500** Governing Capacity (a very large bonus — the legacy no-DLC version only gives +250)
- **−10%** Clergy Influence
- **−10%** Nobility Influence
- **−10%** Burghers Influence

### Special Rules & Mechanics
- 🔒 **Locked government type** — cannot be converted away through normal means (`allow_normal_conversion = no`)
- 🔒 **Tier 1 is locked** once selected (`lock_level_when_selected = yes`) — you cannot swap it out
- 👑 **Fixed rank 3 (Empire)** — your government rank is permanently locked at Empire tier
- ⚔️ **Unify China CB** — grants a permanent Casus Belli to unify the Chinese states
- 🚫 **Cannot force tributaries** via the standard mechanic (China's tribute system uses the Mandate of Heaven mechanics instead)
- 🏛️ **Enables three court factions**: **Temples**, **Eunuchs**, and **Bureaucrats**
- 📦 **90% of territory** is assigned to estates at start (`start_territory_to_estates = 0.9`)
- ✅ **With Mandate of Heaven DLC**: also activates the **Meritocracy** mechanic (the faction system is replaced by Meritocracy)

### Notable Restrictions
- **Autonomy floor of 50%** in owned provinces — you cannot reduce autonomy below 50% (noted in «Art of War» wiki)
- The **Cossacks estate** is unavailable to nations with this reform

---

## Legacy Version (`celestial_empire_legacy`)

There is also a pre-DLC **legacy** version of the reform (for saves from before Mandate of Heaven was introduced). It gives:
- +0.5 Prestige, +250 Governing Capacity (half of the full version)
- +10% Institution Embracement Cost (a drawback the full version doesn't have)
- Same three factions; same fixed empire rank
- Cannot be selected in the nation designer or by new countries

---

## Summary

The Celestial Empire is effectively **Ming's exclusive government form**, tied to holding the **Emperor of China** title (with MoH DLC). Its headline strength is the massive **+500 Governing Capacity** and **estate influence reductions**, which help manage China's enormous territorial size — but the **locked tier and locked government type** mean you have very little flexibility in how you govern. Losing the Mandate of Heaven means losing this reform entirely.
